title: Where delirium screening fails on a geriatric medicine ward: a 12-week prospective observational study
abstract: Objective: to measure delirium screening completion per eligible patient-shift and the time from positive screen to medical review. Design: prospective observational study over 12 weeks on a 28-bed geriatric medicine ward, with daily record reconciliation and direct observation of six shifts a week. Results and conclusions will be written after data collection.
introduction: Delirium screening is required for older inpatients, but completion is rarely measured as it happens, documentation overstates it, and people with dementia are screened least. This study measures where screening fails before any change is made.
methods: All patients aged 65 or over present during a shift were eligible. A research nurse reconciled screening entries with shift lists daily and observed a fixed bed rota on six shifts a week. Completion was estimated with GEE models clustered by patient and reported by six pre-specified factors.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present completion by shift and patient group, the proportion of documented screens confirmed by observation, and time from positive screen to review.
discussion: The discussion will set local completion against the retrieved ward studies and state which failure point the first change should target.
limitations: One ward, observer effect, and dementia status taken from documentation.
conclusion: To be written after the analysis; it will describe where screening fails and will not claim effects of any intervention.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
